title: Customer questions & misconceptions: tool calling + structured output (notes for docs/FAQ)
content:
Purpose
- Capture recurring customer questions (support + sales) about tool calling, structured output, and how they behave with streaming.
- Use this as input for:
  - Docs FAQ + troubleshooting callouts
  - Canonical examples narrative (Python/TS/Go parity)
  - Product messaging/terminology alignment (PM-612)

Where these notes came from (not exhaustive)
- Support tickets: SUP-18421 (disconnects + incomplete tool args), SUP-18433 (schema mismatch from old snippet), SUP-18455 (TS parse error from partial JSON deltas)
- Sales/prospect deep dive: Fireflies 2026-01-22 (streaming + tool semantics questions)
- Customer escalation: Fireflies 2026-02-06 (proxy/load balancer stream disconnects)
- Slack threads: #support corporate proxy issue; #devex tool-call delta edge cases

Terminology that customers confuse (what we should say consistently)
- Tool calling vs function calling
  - Many customers use “function calling” as the generic term; we should prefer “tool calling” in Redwood docs and mention “aka function calling” once early.
- Structured output vs JSON mode
  - Customers often expect “JSON mode” to mean “always valid JSON” without specifying a schema.
  - Our docs should distinguish:
    - “structured output (schema-based)” = model guided by JSON Schema + we validate
    - “JSON output (no schema)” = best-effort JSON; may still be invalid or incomplete

Recurring customer questions (and what they usually actually need)

1) “If I enable structured output, do I still need to validate JSON?”
- What they mean: “Can I stop writing defensive parsing?”
- Key misconception: “Schema mode guarantees validity 100% of the time.”
- Guidance we should include:
  - Always validate on the client side.
  - Plan for retries (or fallback) on:
    - parse errors
    - schema validation errors
    - truncated outputs (esp. timeouts)
  - Provide a minimal, copy/paste validation + retry pattern in each SDK.
- Support impact:
  - SUP-18433: user copied old snippet and assumed schema would be inferred; got mismatch errors.

2) “Why is the model returning the schema back to me / extra fields / commentary?”
- What they mean: “How do I force ‘only JSON’?”
- Typical root causes:
  - Prompt doesn’t clearly say “output must be valid JSON matching the schema”
  - Schema is under-specified (e.g., allowing additionalProperties or missing required fields)
  - Customer is streaming and parsing mid-stream (see streaming section)
- Docs action:
  - Add a short checklist: “tighten schema; require fields; set additionalProperties=false; avoid ambiguous unions where possible.”

3) “Can I stream structured output and parse incrementally?”
- What they mean: “I want to show partial structured data in the UI as it arrives.”
- Reality / gotchas:
  - While streaming, you will see partial JSON that is not parseable.
  - Many customers try to JSON.parse each chunk and either crash or silently discard errors.
  - Tool-call arguments behave similarly: they arrive as deltas.
- Recommended pattern for docs/examples:
  - Accumulate deltas into a buffer.
  - Only parse/validate when we have the final event (or a terminal message).
  - If you must show progress, show raw text/preview but treat it as untrusted until final parse.
- Support impact:
  - SUP-18455: TS parse error caused by parsing partial JSON deltas.

4) “What exactly is a tool call delta? Why are the tool args incomplete?”
- What they mean: “Is this a bug in Redwood?”
- Key misconception: “The gateway should only emit complete tool arguments.”
- Explanation that resonates:
  - Streaming can emit partial arguments. Think of it as incremental assembly; you must concatenate in order.
  - Customers should not dispatch the tool until:
    - tool call is marked complete OR
    - stream ends and final response is received
- Docs action:
  - Add a prominent callout on tool docs page: “tool_call arguments are streamed; do not parse/execute until complete.”
  - Provide a canonical “accumulate by tool_call_id” snippet for Python/TS/Go.

5) “Can the model call multiple tools in parallel? If so, how do I handle it?”
- What they mean: “Do I run them concurrently? In what order do I send results back?”
- Common concerns:
  - Concurrency & rate limits on their own downstream APIs
  - Deterministic ordering / reproducibility
- Recommended docs stance:
  - Yes, parallel tool calls are possible.
  - Provide a concurrency limiter pattern (e.g., max 3 at a time) and clear mapping from tool_call_id -> result.
  - Results should be returned with the matching tool_call_id; ordering should not be assumed.

6) “When should I use tool calling vs structured output?”
- What they mean: “I’m building an agent-ish workflow; what’s the simplest reliable choice?”
- Practical guidance we should put in FAQ:
  - Use tool calling when you need side effects (fetch data, write to DB, call internal services).
  - Use structured output when you want a validated payload (extract entities, normalize inputs, create a typed object).
  - It’s common to combine them: tool call(s) -> then structured output summarization/formatting.

7) “If the schema changes, do old prompts break? How do I version this?”
- What they mean: “How do I roll out safely?”
- Typical failure mode:
  - They change schema required fields and suddenly see schema mismatch errors in production.
- Docs action:
  - Add schema versioning advice:
    - Keep schema version in your app config
    - Roll out with canary; log validation failures
    - Provide a fallback schema or fallback model policy where possible

8) “Why do I get ‘schema mismatch’ or ‘silent parse failure’ without clear remediation?”
- What they mean: “What do I do now?”
- Common gaps:
  - Customers don’t log the raw model output (or they log secrets)
  - Customers swallow JSON.parse exceptions
- Recommended troubleshooting guidance:
  - Log structured error details + a redacted excerpt of output (first/last N chars)
  - Include request_id / trace_id
  - If streaming, persist the assembled buffer on failure
  - Add a single retry with a short corrective instruction (e.g., “Output MUST match schema; no extra keys; no prose.”)

9) “Does structured output guarantee the model won’t hallucinate?”
- What they mean: “Is schema validation a correctness mechanism?”
- Clarify:
  - Schema validation guarantees shape, not truth.
  - If they need factuality, they still need retrieval/verification.

10) “Can I trust tool arguments from the model? Are they safe to execute?”
- What they mean: “Is this secure by default?”
- Key misconception: “If the model says call tool X with args Y, Redwood has vetted it.”
- Security stance to repeat:
  - Tool calling output is untrusted user-controlled content.
  - Require allowlists for tool names.
  - Validate args (types + constraints) before executing.
  - Avoid shell execution / arbitrary URL fetch in examples.
- Action:
  - Ensure all public examples include an allowlist + validation pattern (Marcus requested this explicitly).

11) “My stream disconnects behind our proxy / load balancer. Is streaming reliable?”
- What they mean: “Can I run this in enterprise networks without constant failures?”
- Observed patterns (from support + escalation call):
  - Corporate proxies buffer or terminate long-lived connections
  - Idle timeouts on L7 load balancers
  - Customers using fetch/HTTP clients that don’t support event streams correctly
- Docs action:
  - Add clear mitigations:
    - set client timeouts appropriately
    - prefer direct egress or proxy exceptions for SSE
    - retry/resume guidance (where supported) and idempotency notes
  - Provide a troubleshooting table: symptom -> likely cause -> fix.

12) “How do I test these flows in CI without burning tokens or flaking?”
- What they mean: “I don’t want examples to drift; can we verify?”
- Answer direction:
  - Provide mock server-based snippet tests by default.
  - Optional staging integration tests behind a flag.
  - Emphasize redaction of keys and rate-limit-safe settings.

Quotes/paraphrases that came up repeatedly (useful for FAQ framing)
- “We assumed JSON mode meant it can’t output invalid JSON. Why did it include a sentence at the top?”
- “We’re seeing tool arguments like ‘{\n  \"user_id\": ’ and then nothing. Is that a gateway bug?”
- “We JSON.parse every chunk and it works in dev but fails randomly in prod.”
- “We want parallel tool calls but we need to cap concurrency to protect our internal APIs.”
- “Our proxy kills the stream at ~60 seconds; can you make streaming not require a long-lived connection?”

What we should add to docs (concrete to-dos)
- Streaming page:
  - Callout: “Do not parse JSON until final event; deltas are partial.”
  - Troubleshooting: proxy buffering + timeouts, with recommended client config.
- Tool calling page:
  - Callout: “tool_call deltas; accumulate by id; only execute when complete.”
  - Safe dispatch pattern: allowlist + argument validation.
  - Parallel tools: concurrency limiting + ordering guidance.
- Structured output page:
  - Validation + retry recipe; strict vs lenient parsing guidance.
  - Schema best practices (required fields, additionalProperties=false, avoid overly broad unions).
  - Versioning + rollout guidance.
- SDK guides:
  - Ensure the same narrative across Python/TS/Go.
  - A small “common mistakes” section (copy/paste friendly).

Open questions / things we need Product/Eng to confirm wording for
- Exact user-facing phrasing for “structured output” vs “JSON mode” and where to mention legacy naming.
- Whether we should recommend a standard error taxonomy in docs (e.g., parse_error vs schema_validation_error) vs keeping it high-level.
- Whether we want to document any stream resume semantics explicitly (and if so, what’s guaranteed vs best-effort).

Owner notes (Dev)
- This doc is intentionally rough. Goal is to feed FAQ + troubleshooting, not be a spec.
- Please add new Qs with a short ‘source’ note (ticket/call) so we can measure impact after launch.
